name: The Eroded Anthem

stars.name: Eroded Anthem A
stars.notes: Sol-analogue primary; all five known planets orbit here in stable S-type paths.

stars.name: Eroded Anthem B
stars.notes: Dim companion at roughly 120 AU; its slow orbit frames the outer system like a dying ember.

planets.name: Descant
planets.notes: Sun-baked rock with no recorded landing; sensor sweeps return flat silence.

planets.name: Fermata
planets.notes: Cratered regolith world once shortlisted for a listening post that was never built.

planets.name: Tacet
planets.notes: Pale-striped giant anchoring the patrol station's orbit; its gravity well shields the wormhole approach lanes.

planets.name: Obsequy
planets.notes: Fractured ice shell suggesting an ancient subsurface ocean, long since frozen and unexamined.

planets.name: Reprise
planets.notes: Outermost world, drifting near the binary barycenter's tidal boundary and slowly perturbed across millennia.

anomalies.name: Cerulean Tithe
anomalies.notes: A stable wormhole mouth linking the Antiphon Gap to two distant sectors; whoever holds this system holds the crossing, which is why the navy patrols an otherwise empty sky.

stations.name: Anthem Watch
stations.notes: Concord naval outpost monitoring the Tithe approach lanes; its garrison rotates every six months and counts itself fortunate to leave.

stations.name: Tithe Point Observatory
stations.notes: Instrumentation platform measuring the wormhole's throat geometry under naval escort; its findings are sealed.

faction_control.notes: The Concord Navy enforces a strict transit regime around the Cerulean Tithe while scavenger flotillas and two rival powers probe the perimeter for gaps in the watch.

history: First charted as a curiosity of a yellow-red binary with nothing worth naming until the Cerulean Tithe was found holding station at the system's edge.
A brief standoff three decades ago between Concord pickets and a corporate exploration wing ended with the navy's claim affirmed and the observatory established.
Transit through the Tithe is now limited to sanctioned convoys, though smuggler charts circulate claiming windows when the patrol thins.
description: A yellow primary and its small red companion wheel about one another over five uninhabited worlds, their combined light falling on ice and bare rock with perfect indifference. Nothing in the system was built by nature to draw attention, yet at its far edge the Cerulean Tithe hangs open, a blue-lit throat in space. The contrast between the quiet middle system and the instrumented outer dark is the first thing every visitor notices.

The system's value is entirely positional: the wormhole connects three sectors, and the Concord Navy maintains Anthem Watch and a sealed research platform to keep the crossing accountable to no one else. Traffic is light but deliberate, made up of patrol cycles, sanctioned convoys, and resupply runs, each transit logged and escorted. No civilian settlement has ever been permitted.

Rival powers continue to test whether the patrol can be stretched thin, and salvagers whisper of hulls lost inside the Tithe that never came out the documented far side. The observatory's sealed findings fuel speculation that the throat is widening or wandering toward the inner system. Service at Anthem Watch is described in naval circles as quiet duty with a long memory.
